correctness.rationale: Truncated strong laws on a countable set of truncation levels force the observed sample mean to diverge, so the fitted shape converges to 1 from above. The fitted CDF varies uniformly near 1 (its shape derivative is bounded by sup over x≥1 of x^(-1/2)log x on a neighborhood of 1). Glivenko–Cantelli gives the uniform observed discrepancy limit; maximizing x^(-β)-x^(-1) gives x*=β^(-1/(1−β)) and dβ as stated. The CvM integrand converges uniformly to the square of a bounded continuous function, so one can also pass to the weak limit of the fitted integration measure. The substitution u=1/x gives cβ=2(1−β)^2/[3(β+2)(2β+1)], as obtained from the three displayed fractions. Conditional on almost every data path, each bootstrap row has its own fitted shape. For any fixed K, choose a common finite L with the truncated mean at shape 1 greater than 2K; continuity gives mean >3K/2 along the row sequence eventually. Bounded concentration gives row-average truncations >K with probability tending to one, without any triangular-array untruncated LLN. Thus the bootstrap refit also converges to 1, and distribution-free DKW shows D*n→0 in conditional probability and W*n/n≤(D*n)^2→0. Nonnegativity and any fixed upper quantile level strictly between 0 and 1 imply the quantile limits, hence eventual rejection almost surely on those paths. This verifies the stated known endpoint, fixed subunit shape, and ideal conditional refitting only. Independently checked d(1/2)=1/4 and c(1/2)=1/30 exactly; a bounded illustration sampled X=(1−U)^(-2) with 24 independently refitted bootstrap replicates per n using U uniform. At n=4000 and 50000 the observed (KS,CvM/n) were (0.262197,0.034498) and (0.248342,0.033061), against empirical .95 bootstrap pairs (0.059398,0.001488) and (0.040694,0.000834). Replay with NumPy default_rng(5015), sorted fitted CDF values u_i, one-sided KS jump-end formulas, and CvM/n=mean((u_i−(i−1/2)/n)^2)+1/(12n²). The uploaded checker was read, not run; its shape grid and special-case tolerances are floating-point and its simulated statistic is KS only. Those observations do not affect the exact theorem.

evidence: The comparative paper notes the finite-mean restriction and reports departure from nominal size at shape 1; the thesis's incorporated comparison has a corresponding discussion.
Ordinary EDF consistency under fixed discrepancy does not itself control the conditional law of each refitted bootstrap row with an approaching shape.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known moment obstruction identifies why a fit can accumulate at 1, but the near-1 simulation-row model has a mean that depends on n. The exact conditional claim uses an additional fixed-truncation argument and distribution-free concentration, not a fixed-model consistency corollary.

evidence: The earlier studies provide the estimator, observed size problems at the boundary, or the resampling convention, not a fixed-subunit-shape conditional comparison. At the earlier reported boundary β=1 the two claimed positive observed limits would instead be zero.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: There is no transfer of the boundary simulations to the fixed-subunit theorem: the positive limiting bias, the triangular bootstrap limit, and the quantile comparison have different roles and are all established in the frozen proof.

evidence: The 2023 Fourier preprint uses a known endpoint of 1, a composite null with β>0, and the same fit Xbar/(Xbar−1). Its Section 4 uses pooled warp-speed calibration for simulation.
The 2022 comparison distinguishes the fixed-endpoint and estimated-endpoint problems; Sections 2.1 and 3.2 give the EDF definitions and moment fit/bootstrap.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This is equivalently a nonvanishing observed-to-fitted EDF gap paired with a vanishing conditional bootstrap gap after normalization, or a size-one pointwise null rejection result. Same-model simulations and a warp-speed calibration scheme do not state the latter result for ideal conditional quantiles.

value.rationale: For genuine heavy-tail null data, nominal calibration can fail as badly as possible even when every repetition refits. The two distinct exact EDF gaps and the conditional control distinguish this diagnostic from a generic warning about infinite means and specify which fitting workflow to avoid. It does not diagnose MLE, Fourier tests or boundary shape 1.
